DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel` silently treats missing failure probabilities as `0.0`. If the caller supplies only one override, or a class member has no stored base rate, both `pairwise_joint_failure()` and `correlated_class_failure()` can collapse to zero risk instead of rejecting incomplete inputs. I reproduced `pairwise_joint_failure("m1","m2", p_i=0.2) == 0.0` and `correlated_class_failure(["m1","m2"], {"m1": 0.2}) == 0.0` with `v_12 = 0.9`. That turns partial telemetry into a false “safe” estimate.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require a validated failure rate for every referenced model, or raise on missing rates instead of defaulting to zero.

LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py:2711](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2711), [dynamic_management.py:2748](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2748)  
DESCRIPTION: The correlated-failure APIs bypass probability-range validation on override inputs. `set_base_failure_rate()` enforces `[0,1]`, but direct `p_i`/`p_j` and `failure_rates` values are trusted raw. I reproduced `pairwise_joint_failure("m1","m2", p_i=1.2, p_j=1.2) == 1.2`; negative overrides can likewise return negative outputs because the final clamp is only `min(...)`. This breaks the stated probability contract and can poison any dispatch logic that assumes a real probability.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate all override probabilities into `[0,1]` and clamp final results to `[0,1]`.

LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py:2256](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2256)  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` misclassifies improving negative `mu` as a pathology. The check `recent_mu[i + 1] > recent_mu[i] * 1.1` assumes positive values; with negative marginal values, moving from `-10` to `-7` to `-5` satisfies the predicate and emits a `"mu increasing"` diagnosis even though the system is recovering toward zero loss. I reproduced that exact sequence with stable finding counts and got a false warning.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use signed-delta logic, or only apply the multiplicative growth test when both compared `mu` values are positive.

LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py:2205](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2205), [dynamic_management.py:2256](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2256), [dynamic_management.py:2293](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2293)  
DESCRIPTION: The advertised adaptive immune-response mechanism is only wired for `kappa`. `effective_window()` is written as if every detector participates in `_pathology_counts` / `_resolved_counts`, but only the `kappa` branch ever mutates those maps; the `mu` and `mu+novelty` branches never record persistence or resolution. I reproduced repeated `mu` pathologies over four rounds and both maps stayed empty while severity remained `WARNING` every time. So the monitor’s “adaptive sensitivity” claim does not hold for most of the health layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Route all detector branches through one shared persistence/resolution update path, or narrow the documented claim to `kappa` only.
